# ENERGY — sector digest, ISO week 2026-W44

**Coverage published.** The desk's coal and coal-logistics wave went live this week: 21 names now carry published coverage [coverage index]. Five BUY — AADI 12,399, BBRM 158, DWGL 428, KKGI 374, PTBA 5,112. Four HOLD — BSSR 4,408, GEMS 6,762, ITMG 21,534, MBAP 1,658. Five REDUCE — ADMR 1,058, ALII 516, BUMI 124, BYAN 7,142, IATA 72. Six SELL — ARII 306, BESS 185, GTBO 53, INDY 1,256, SGER 124, SMMT 1,615. BOSS.JK is NOT RATED, published as a fundamental-value marker for a suspended non-filer.

**Changes.** ADMR moved to REDUCE from SELL after D&A-anchoring sustaining capex and restating FY2025 net debt. ITMG moved to HOLD: on a six-month realised-price basis the dividend no longer covers the premium over economic-life value. PTBA held BUY through its 9M print, treating the DSI channel as a risk rather than a booked shock. BYAN reset FY2026E to the 30 October 9M LK.

**Deck moves.** The coal deck was signed off with sourced actuals: Newcastle FY2025A 108.4 and FY2024A 136.1 [S23, World Bank Pink Sheet], spot 150.35; HBA 126.81 with HBA I/II/III at 93.62/66.10/45.53 [S25/S24]; DMO cap 70 [S6]; IUPK royalty as HBA-band fractions from PP 18/2025 [S15/S35]. ICI-3 and ICI-4 remain needs_source. The oil deck carries Brent spot 112.79 (30 Oct) against an 84 FY2027E path [oil deck], so the war premium is priced far above the reversion anchor.

**Material news.** PTBA 9M net profit Rp4.41trn, +216% y/y; BYAN 9M +12.9% to US$589.6m at a 35.5% gross margin; government mandates all coal exports through state exporter PT DSI from 1 January 2027, with APBI warning of disruption; BUMI closed Mount Margaret (US$22m); OJK fines tied to BREN/DSSA/CUAN reached Rp2.1trn; MBSS won a five-year GEL coal-transport contract worth up to Rp6trn [news triage 2026-10-29/30].

**Watch next week.** DSI implementation detail and any service fee; whether the Brent spot-versus-path gap persists; post-review revisions in ITMG, BYAN and PTBA; and the remaining queued initiations (PTRO, SINI, RAJA, RATU, ENRG and the coal-logistics names).

*Research only; not a recommendation to act.*
